summary: Phase 8 group-booking PAYMENT MODEL resolved earlier (single-payer, exclusive-only, unified surcharge pricing). 2026-07-27: OCCUPANCY MODEL now also resolved — occupancy type is a host-set, per-listing property with THREE modes (exclusive / drop-in-common-use / open-play-cost-split) that split into different phases because they add complexity in different subsystems. Phase 8 = exclusive-only, unchanged.

resolved_design.single_payer: Organizer pays for ALL pax. Exactly one payment -> reuses the existing hold-until-session rail unchanged (no cost-splitting, no per-attendee collection). This is what makes it buildable.
resolved_design.two_axes: Pricing unit (per-space flat vs per-head) x Occupancy (exclusive vs open). These are independent; earlier discussion conflated them.
resolved_design.v1_scope: EXCLUSIVE-ONLY. Group booking = one exclusive lock on the space -> existing GiST exclusion constraint untouched.
resolved_design.open_play_deferred: Open court / open play (strangers share one slot, each pays per head) is a SEPARATE future product. [2026-07-27 refinement: this 'strangers share, each pays per head' actually splits in TWO — the HOST-RUN capacity-counter version = the DROP-IN/COMMON-USE mode (its own future phase), while the ORGANIZER-driven version = open-play/cost-split (GPAY-01) which PRESERVES the exclusion constraint. See occupancy_model.] Do NOT build either in v1.
resolved_design.unified_pricing_formula: total = baseRate + max(0, pax - included) * extraHeadFee. extraHeadFee=0 => flat court rental, zero leak, backward-compatible default (existing listings unchanged). included+fee => group size affects price, leak bounded to surcharge delta. 'per-person' = the extreme (included=1) => max under-declaration exposure, front desk is the enforcement. This is the Airbnb extra-guest-fee shape.
resolved_design.scope_reach: Reaches into Phase 2 (host sets base + optional included/extraHeadFee) and Phase 4 (quote applies the formula), but shallow + backward-compatible because extraHeadFee defaults to 0.

occupancy_model.principle: Occupancy type is a first-class HOST-SET, per-listing property. Three modes; the older 'open play = GPAY-02 (breaks the exclusion constraint)' lump was too coarse and splits in two.

exclusive.examples: basketball, exclusive pickleball court, gym/studio buyout

drop_in_common_use.availability: capacity-counter (NEW — count-then-insert seat race, the anti-pattern the exclusion constraint was built to avoid)
drop_in_common_use.payment: single-payer PER BOOKING (already built — each visitor books their own head(s); NO multi-payer, NO RSVP, NO ticketing)
drop_in_common_use.examples: common-use / drop-in gym, host-run open court
drop_in_common_use.status: OWN future phase — NOT part of Phase 8; roadmap follow-up owed via /gsd-phase

open_play_cost_split.availability: GiST exclusion constraint (already built — organizer holds ONE exclusive lock)
open_play_cost_split.examples: organizer opens their own booked slot to others
open_play_cost_split.status: future GPAY-01, ORGANIZER-driven; builds on Phase 8 RSVP shell

occupancy_model.key_insight: Drop-in gym is NOT open play. Drop-in stresses AVAILABILITY (needs the capacity-counter) but keeps payment simple; open play stresses PAYMENT (cost-split) but keeps availability exclusive. Different subsystems -> different phases.
occupancy_model.phase8_impact: Phase 8 stays exclusive-only but records a host-set occupancy_mode on the listing, DEFAULT 'exclusive' — the seam both future modes plug into. Q-18 answered = option a (per-attendee RSVP rows, payment-ready but unpriced) because the future paid version is organizer-driven cost-split (GPAY-01).

headcount_model.rsvp_cap_source: RSVP hard cap = the listing's maxOccupancy, which is ALREADY a required publish field (publishSchema requires z.number().int().positive(); src/lib/validation/listing.ts:69). Every group-bookable (published) listing therefore has a positive capacity, so the Q-06 'NULL capacity' premise is FACTUALLY STALE — the NULL branch is a defensive guard for drafts/legacy rows only, never a product path. maxOccupancy has been a required-but-DORMANT field since Phase 2 (collected + displayed, never enforced in booking); Phase 8 is its first consumer, Phase 9 makes it load-bearing.
headcount_model.snapshot: Freeze the cap onto the GROUP row at group-creation (capacity_snapshot); the RSVP path reads ONLY the snapshot, never live listing.maxOccupancy. A host editing capacity down after attendees confirm cannot retroactively over-cap them — the retroactive-overflow bug becomes structurally unrepresentable. Mirrors the D-77 (cancellation tier) / WR-06 (full_day) snapshot pattern. Distinct from declaredPax, which freezes at BOOKING time and drives price; capacity_snapshot freezes at GROUP-creation and drives RSVP.
headcount_model.atomic_enforcement: SC#4 'atomic, no overflow' enforced by a pessimistic 'SELECT capacity_snapshot FROM group WHERE id=? FOR UPDATE' seat-claim inside the RSVP transaction: count current 'yes' rows under that lock, insert the yes only if count < snapshot, else reject 'full'. NOT an unlocked count-then-insert (the CLAUDE.md anti-pattern) — the FOR UPDATE lock on the single group row is the authority, analogous to the GiST exclusion constraint for the exclusive lock. Handles yes<->no toggles uniformly (every transition goes through the same guarded path). PROVEN by a two-connection boundary race test (makeRacingClients, like Phase 3 SC#4) = the plan's acceptance gate. Denormalized-counter alternative DEFERRED to Phase 9 (much higher contention: a shared slot across many independent bookings, where a per-parent lock is too coarse).
headcount_model.organizer_and_counting: Organizer is attendee #1 — counted in both the cap and declaredPax; pricing included=1 = the organizer's seat folded into base. Only confirmed 'yes' RSVPs consume a seat; 'no'/unanswered consume nothing; a partial RSVP leaves the booking valid (Q-07a / Q-08a / Q-09a).
headcount_model.declaredpax_signal: declaredPax (the paid baseline) vs RSVP: RSVP-yes exceeding declaredPax = a corroboration flag + top-up nudge (a SIGNAL, never a block). The entire declaredPax/top-up/corroboration machinery only activates when extraHeadFee > 0; flat listings (extraHeadFee=0, the default) carry none of it — group booking there is just exclusive-lock + RSVP-capped-at-capacity.
headcount_model.why_cap_at_capacity_not_paid_pax: RSVP is voluntary and unpaid, so it is NOT the leak-enforcement lever — a freeloader just shows up without RSVPing. Capping RSVP at paid-pax buys zero revenue protection and only (a) frustrates honest friends and (b) destroys the corroboration signal (RSVP could never exceed paid, so under-declaration is undetectable). The leak is caught at host check-in headcount + top-up, never at the RSVP gate. So the cap is the loosest thing consistent with physical reality = maxOccupancy.

rsvp_model.note: All 12 open 08-QUESTIONS.json gray areas RESOLVED 2026-07-27 (raw answers saved in 08-QUESTIONS.json). Load-bearing synthesis below; the rest are the recommended options.
rsvp_model.identity_HYBRID: Q-02 landed as a HYBRID (guest-or-login), modeled as ONE rsvp row with a NULLABLE user_id (NOT two subsystems). Login/sign-up -> user_id set -> in-app + email notifications, verified identity. Guest -> user_id null, self-typed name + OPTIONAL email. GROUP-03 STAYS UNCHANGED — the guest path satisfies 'RSVP without needing a full account', so NO requirement reversal (the earlier 'account required' framing from the raw Q-02 note is superseded).
rsvp_model.guest_email_optional: Guest email is OPTIONAL. Blank -> headcount-only, no platform comms (a blank-email guest cannot toggle their RSVP and gets no cancellation notice — the organizer's own group chat covers them). Email provided -> RSVP confirmation + cancellation notice (Q-13) + a self-serve manage link to change the answer (Q-03) — but NO reminders. The account path is the 'be kept in the loop' path; that is the deliberate incentive to sign up.
rsvp_model.v1_simplifications: No guest email verification; no guest->account merge; opt-in email guard (only ever email an address that submitted an RSVP on the link, rate-limited, so an invite link can't be turned into a spam cannon); de-dup by user_id (accounts) / normalized email (guests who gave one). name-only guests are intentionally not de-dupable/toggle-able.
rsvp_model.invites_Q01: Shareable link ONLY (one group link; NO per-recipient email invites in v1). A recipient opens the link -> RSVPs as guest or logs in.
rsvp_model.lifecycle_answers: Q-03 toggle yes/no until close (accounts + guests-with-email via the self-serve link; blank-email guests can't). Q-04 one person = one RSVP, no +guests. Q-10 'Invite people' affordance on the confirmed booking detail page. Q-11 any confirmed (paid) booking qualifies (instant or request; exclusive-mode only per the occupancy model). Q-12 RSVP closes at session start. Q-13 on booking cancel/refund -> auto-void invites + notify attendees (accounts + guests-with-email; blank-email guests not reachable). Q-14 organizer can revoke invite / remove attendee / resend + regenerate link. Q-15 NO attendee reminders in v1 (organizer keeps the existing Phase-7 booking reminders). Q-16 attendee sees venue name + date/time + address per listing.showExactAddress. Q-17 organizer notified per RSVP (in-app + email) + attendee gets an RSVP confirmation (in-app/email for accounts, email for guests-who-gave-email, on-screen only for blank-email guests).

money_leak_analysis.crux: per-person-exclusive is the most-exposed cell: organizer declares pax=1, pays for 1, brings 4 (court is already theirs, no stranger blocked, only the front desk forces honesty).
money_leak_analysis.structural_truth: Leak is proportional to how much price depends on door-counted heads: per-space=0, surcharge=bounded, pure per-head=max. per-head-exclusive CANNOT be made self-policing without becoming ticketing (the deferred open-play model).
mitigations_settled: Structurally prefer per-space + surcharge (bounds exposure to the surcharge delta).
Host check-in headcount confirmation -> creates a discrepancy RECORD (v1 seam) + enables an in-app TOP-UP charge to organizer's saved card (top-up = fast-follow).
RSVP shell doubles as a fraud-corroboration signal (RSVP count vs declared pax mismatch = flag) -> gives invites a hard job beyond logistics.
Align host incentives so they don't prefer cash (payout / ranking / dispute protection flow only from on-platform bookings).
Accept the bounded remainder, priced into commission (every marketplace leaks at the last mile).

refund_no_show: Organizer bought the slots -> no per-attendee refund on no-shows. pax-decrease follows the Phase-7 cancellation ladder; pax-increase = capacity-checked top-up.

human_actions_pending.action: Pre-launch money-loop validation vs PayMongo test mode (payment -> confirm -> payout -> refund)
human_actions_pending.context: Separate track, unchanged. Never driven end-to-end. Card/GCash testable now (fixture booking 42132ab1 / pay_C4PW6fRGtUTNm6GsKCpt4P36); QRPh + payout blocked on PayMongo Money Movement beta.

decisions.decision: v1 group bookings = single-payer (organizer pays all pax), exclusive-only, reusing the existing payment rail
decisions.rationale: One payment sidesteps the cost-splitting complexity that got other models rejected; exclusive lock keeps the exclusion constraint intact

decisions.decision: Unified exclusive pricing: base + optional per-extra-head surcharge over an included headcount; extraHeadFee defaults to 0
decisions.rationale: Airbnb extra-guest-fee shape; makes group size affect price (answers the 'feels free' complaint) while staying backward-compatible and bounding the leak

decisions.decision: Open play / open court DEFERRED to its own future phase
decisions.rationale: = GPAY-02 ticketing + capacity-counter availability; would break the GiST exclusion constraint and needs per-attendee payment

decisions.decision: Per-person-exclusive under-declaration leak accepted as bounded-by-design
decisions.rationale: Cannot be made self-policing without becoming ticketing; mitigated via prefer-per-space, host check-in record + top-up (fast-follow), RSVP corroboration, incentive alignment, commission buffer

decisions.decision: (2026-07-27) Occupancy type is a host-set, per-listing property with THREE modes (exclusive / drop-in-common-use / open-play-cost-split)
decisions.rationale: The modes add complexity in different subsystems (availability vs payment), so they belong in different phases; the old 'open play = GPAY-02' lump conflated a host-run capacity-counter with organizer-run cost-split

decisions.decision: (2026-07-27) Phase 8 stays exclusive-only and records occupancy_mode (default 'exclusive') on the listing
decisions.rationale: Keeps Phase 8 inside the existing exclusion-constraint + single-payer rails while leaving the seam future modes plug into

decisions.decision: (2026-07-27) Drop-in / common-use (per-head, host-run, capacity-counter) gets its own dedicated roadmap phase, not folded into Phase 8
decisions.rationale: Keeps per-head gyms first-class without dragging the count-then-insert seat-race (the anti-pattern the exclusion constraint avoids) onto Phase 8's money path; drop-in needs new AVAILABILITY only, payment stays single-payer-per-booking

decisions.decision: (2026-07-27) Open play's future = organizer-driven cost-split (GPAY-01), so Phase 8 RSVP schema uses per-attendee rows (Q-18 = a)
decisions.rationale: Organizer-driven cost-split preserves the exclusion constraint and plugs directly into the RSVP shell; per-attendee rows let a future price attach one-to-one with no reshape

decisions.decision: (2026-07-27) RSVP hard cap = the listing's maxOccupancy (already a required publish field), SNAPSHOTTED onto the group row at group-creation (capacity_snapshot); RSVP never reads live listing capacity
decisions.rationale: Kills the retroactive-overflow bug (host lowering capacity under confirmed attendees) by making it structurally unrepresentable; mirrors the D-77 / full_day snapshot pattern

decisions.decision: (2026-07-27) No-overflow enforced by a 'SELECT ... FOR UPDATE' seat-claim on the group row inside the RSVP txn (NOT unlocked count-then-insert), proven by a makeRacingClients boundary race test
decisions.rationale: The row lock is the atomic authority (analogous to the GiST exclusion constraint for the exclusive lock) and satisfies SC#4 'atomic, no overflow'; the race test is the plan's acceptance gate. Denormalized-counter alternative deferred to Phase 9's higher-contention capacity-counter

decisions.decision: (2026-07-27) RSVP identity = HYBRID guest-or-login, one rsvp row with a nullable user_id; GROUP-03 stays UNCHANGED (no requirement reversal)
decisions.rationale: The guest path satisfies 'RSVP without a full account' so the locked requirement holds; a nullable user_id keeps it ONE table/one cap-claim/one who's-coming list, with only the notification channel branching (in-app+email for accounts, email/none for guests) — avoids the two-subsystem balloon

decisions.decision: (2026-07-27) Guest email is OPTIONAL: blank = headcount-only (no toggle, no cancel notice); provided = RSVP confirmation + cancellation notice + self-serve toggle link, NO reminders
decisions.rationale: Maximizes conversion (no forced signup wall) while still capturing account-linked identity when available; the account path is the deliberate 'be kept in the loop' incentive. v1: no guest email verification, no guest->account merge, opt-in email guard, de-dup by user_id/normalized email

decisions.decision: (2026-07-27) All 12 remaining 08-QUESTIONS.json gray areas resolved (raw answers in 08-QUESTIONS.json): invites = shareable link only (Q-01); toggle-until-session-start (Q-03/Q-12); one-person-one-RSVP (Q-04); 'Invite people' on booking detail (Q-10); any confirmed paid booking (Q-11); auto-void+notify on cancel (Q-13); organizer manage/revoke/resend/regenerate (Q-14); no attendee reminders v1 (Q-15); address per showExactAddress (Q-16); organizer per-RSVP notify + attendee confirmation (Q-17)
decisions.rationale: Completes the Phase 8 discussion; ready to write 08-CONTEXT.md

next_action: ALL Phase 8 discussion questions RESOLVED (2026-07-27): pricing + occupancy + headcount (headcount_model above) + all 12 RSVP/identity/lifecycle gray areas (rsvp_model above; raw answers in 08-QUESTIONS.json). NEXT: write 08-CONTEXT.md folding in the pricing model, the host-set occupancy_mode seam (exclusive-only), the headcount cap (maxOccupancy snapshot + FOR UPDATE seat-claim + race test), the hybrid guest-or-login identity model (nullable user_id, optional guest email), and the lifecycle answers — then plan Phase 8. Phase 9 (open-capacity/drop-in) is on the roadmap (commit ef53fd2) and plans AFTER Phase 8.
context_notes: STALE-FRAMING WARNING: 08-QUESTIONS.json's top-level framing ('v1 = a FREE RSVP coordination shell') is PARTIALLY STALE — pricing is pax-scaled at booking (still single-payer, still NOT per-attendee collection). Also STALE: Q-06's premise that maxOccupancy is 'NOT required at publish, so many listings have no capacity' — it IS required at publish (publishSchema), so every group-bookable listing has a positive capacity; the NULL branch is defensive-only. 2026-07-27 UPDATES: (1) occupancy is a host-set 3-mode property; Phase 8 = exclusive mode only; drop-in/common-use gyms are a SEPARATE phase (Phase 9, added), NOT the same as open play (organizer-driven cost-split = GPAY-01, exclusion-preserving). (2) Headcount RESOLVED: cap = maxOccupancy snapshotted onto the group row; FOR UPDATE seat-claim + race test; organizer = attendee #1; declaredPax is the paid baseline and RSVP-over-paid is a corroboration/top-up SIGNAL (only when extraHeadFee>0), never a block. Driven as a founder-debate: the user confirmed the 3-mode split, that capacity must be host-set (it already is), the snapshot + FOR UPDATE mechanism, and open play's organizer-driven future.
